section_summary: This section continues a U.S. foreign-broadcast monitoring report on Japanese wartime economic mobilization, shipping, labor, agriculture, and industrial development across Japan and its occupied territories. It analyzes Axis propaganda concerning Free China, relations with the United States, conflict between the Chongqing government and Chinese Communists, and the administration and exploitation of occupied China. The concluding pages survey agricultural production, transportation shortages, industrial expansion, resource development, and infrastructure projects in Manchukuo.

subfiles.title: Radio Report: Japanese Economic Developments, Free China, Occupied China, and Manchuria (continuation)
subfiles.about: A continuing analytical digest of Japanese, Axis, Chongqing, and collaborationist broadcasts concerning wartime economic mobilization and political conditions in China, Japan, Southeast Asia, and Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: The report first surveys Japanese claims about economic collaboration, resource extraction, food production, industrial labor, shipping, and shipbuilding throughout the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere. Its Free China section analyzes propaganda about Sino-American relations, the U.S. immigration exclusion laws, and an alleged political and military crisis between the Chongqing government and the Chinese Communists. The occupied-China section covers concessions and extraterritoriality, collaborationist administration, economic exploitation, military defections, North–Central China relations, and conditions in Shanghai. The final section reviews Manchukuo's agricultural quotas, transport shortages, industrial transfers, mining controls, hydroelectric development, and other resource projects.
